```sql
WITH base AS MATERIALIZED (
    SELECT pv.product_id,
           pv.id AS variant_id,
           ol.order_id,
           ol.quantity,
           ol.line_total_cents
      FROM order_lines ol
      JOIN orders o            ON o.id = ol.order_id
      JOIN product_variants pv ON pv.id = ol.variant_id::uuid
     WHERE o.tenant_id = %(tenant_id)s
       AND o.created_at >= %(from)s
       AND o.created_at <  %(to)s
       AND o.status IN ('paid', 'processing', 'shipped', 'delivered')
),
per_variant AS (
    SELECT product_id,
           count(*)                AS variant_count,
           sum(q)::bigint          AS quantity,
           sum(r)                  AS revenue_cents
      FROM (SELECT product_id, variant_id,
                   sum(quantity)         AS q,
                   sum(line_total_cents) AS r
              FROM base
             GROUP BY product_id, variant_id) v
     GROUP BY product_id
),
per_order AS (
    SELECT product_id, count(*) AS order_count
      FROM (SELECT DISTINCT product_id, order_id FROM base) d
     GROUP BY product_id
)
SELECT p.id,
       p.sku,
       p.name,
       p.brand,
       p.currency,
       po.order_count,
       v.quantity,
       v.revenue_cents,
       v.variant_count
  FROM per_variant v
  JOIN per_order po ON po.product_id = v.product_id
  JOIN products p   ON p.id = v.product_id
 ORDER BY v.quantity DESC, v.revenue_cents DESC
 LIMIT %(limit)s
```

De twee `count(DISTINCT ...)`'s dwongen een grote sortering op (p.id, o.id) af, die naar schijf ging (external merge). Nu worden ze vervangen door hash-aggregaties op (product, variant) en (product, order) over één gematerialiseerde basisset. Daarna wordt pas op het eind met de kleine `products`-tabel gejoind. De types blijven gelijk aan het origineel: `quantity` wordt teruggecast naar bigint en `revenue_cents` blijft numeric.
